abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (TH1)-like immune architectures in mismatch repair-deficient tumors associated with response to anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T-dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4+ T cells differentiated into TH1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r+ early effector CD4+ intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with TH1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ-dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8+ effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4+ T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.
hook: Boosting CD4 T cells with OX40 and PD-1 drugs curbs hard-to-treat colorectal tumors in mice.
summary: Imaging of patient tumors showed Th1-like immune patterns in tumors that respond to anti-PD-1, while proficient tumors had regulatory T cell dominance. In mouse models, combining an OX40 agonist with PD-1 blockade expanded early effector CD4 cells in lymph nodes and brought in CD8 killer cells. The treatment effect is shown only in mice.
title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4+ T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer.
